findings.claim: The casual jargon sweep moves displaced technical content 'into target/anchor/code/snippet fields', but a proposal's only `anchor` field is `gate.anchor` (internal/proposals/proposals.go:49-53), the ACDSL anchor regex smine-apply turns into the authored rule line. On a casual install, a mutable context proposal with gate {band: A, verifier: <registry entry>, anchor: "^internal/.*\.go$"} whose change cites a rule ID or path is reworded and the ID/path lands in gate.anchor, so smine-apply step 4(a) appends a rule that governs the wrong files or none. correctness-5 requires gate fields never be translated or reworded. The same sink wording sits in the casual rules of smine-context/memory/routines/skills L33 and in smine-orchestrate L40.
findings.fix: Replace 'target/anchor/code/snippet fields' with 'snippet code or a fields[] entry labelled technical' in smine-consolidate L51 (and the casual bullets of smine-context/memory/routines/skills L33 and smine-orchestrate L40), and add: never write to gate.* or target during the sweep.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-consolidate SKILL.md L51 (sweep moves content into target/anchor/code/snippet fields), proposals.go L31-53 (Proposal has no top-level anchor or code; Gate.Anchor is 'the anchor the rule would govern'), smine-context L60 (F/A/D proposals name an anchor regex) and smine-apply L31 step 4(a)/(b) (the gate route authors the rule line; (b) dry-run speaks of 'the anchor'). The sweep's only `anchor` destination is that machine-read regex, and correctness-5 (spec-1) says gate fields are never reworded.

findings.claim: smine-apply's permissions branch (L31) takes the rule to append from the proposal's `change` ('the allowlist string named in its change'), and smine-permissions L33 keeps the rule string in `change` on casual installs. The consolidate casual sweep (L51) has no such carve-out, and neither does the orchestrate casual gate (L40), which fixes violations as 'small defects'. Sequence on a casual install: smine-permissions writes change "Add `Bash(gh pr view *)` to `permissions.allow` in settings/claude_code/settings.json" (its own L48 template). The nightly consolidate sees a file path plus `permissions.allow` jargon in `change` and rewords it to plain prose, moving the technical content out. After a + vote, smine-apply finds no rule string in `change` and cannot apply the voted rule as written.
findings.fix: In smine-consolidate §4 (and the smine-orchestrate L40 casual gate), exempt permissions proposals: the rule string stays verbatim in `change` and only the path/jargon around it is reworded. Alternatively, have smine-permissions store the rule in a dedicated field and point smine-apply L31 at that field.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-permissions L33 (casual: 'the rule string itself stays in change') and L48 (the change template carries a file path and permissions.allow), smine-consolidate L51 (the sweep rewords `change` on file paths or schema jargon, with no kind exemption, and its mutable set is all of proposals/*.json per L12), smine-orchestrate L40 (same field list, no exemption) and smine-apply L31 (the permissions branch reads the rule string from `change`). The only stage that knows the rule must stay in `change` is the producer.

findings.claim: Step 3 promises that a rule parked in settings.disabled.json (one the user deliberately turned off) never resurfaces. It reads that file as the sibling of `settings/claude_code/settings.json`, i.e. settings/claude_code/settings.disabled.json, which does not exist in the repo or in any routine worktree. The config server parks rules in the sibling of the live settings file: config.DisabledPath(~/.claude/settings.json) = ~/.claude/settings.disabled.json (cmd/configserver/main.go:42, server.go:284). Sequence: the user parks `Bash(gh pr view *)` on the permissions page, two later sessions prompt and grant it, and the nightly smine-permissions run proposes it again. The promised suppression never fires.
findings.fix: Read the parked rules from ~/.claude/settings.disabled.json (the live settings sibling the config server writes, config.DisabledPath), not from settings/claude_code/.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-permissions L55, then confirmed with `git ls-files settings/claude_code` (no settings.disabled.json; .gitignore does not list it, so a worktree never has it). internal/config/config.go:185-193 puts DisabledPath next to the settings path, whose default is ~/.claude/settings.json (cmd/configserver/main.go:42), and server.go:278-297 loads and saves the parked sidecar there.

findings.claim: On a casual install, the step-4 casual lockout only sets disposition `casual-locked`. The proposal keeps status `proposed`, gets no autoApplyHeld, and is never removed. Step 5 auto-apply (decide is the casual default) makes every remaining `proposed` entry a candidate, and SAFE candidates become implicit + votes filling the cap slots before step 4's lockout fires. So the same locked edit proposal is re-picked every night: a casual-locked line is appended to votes-archive.jsonl and .routine-commit-body each run, and with up to 3 locked entries first in JSON order the cap is consumed with nothing implemented. Locked entries reach skills.json in two ways: they predate a switch to casual, which smine-skills step 3 never drops (its lockout only filters new candidates, L45), or smine-consolidate §2 re-homes them into skills.json with no lockout.
findings.fix: In smine-apply step 5, exclude candidates the casual lockout would block before they claim a cap slot, and write autoApplyHeld {reason: "casual-locked"}. Also have smine-skills step 3 reconciliation drop `proposed` edit entries that target a skill without `origin: user` on casual installs.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-apply L31 (lockout sets the disposition only), L32 (candidates are every remaining `proposed` entry), L35-36 (SAFE candidates become implicit + votes filling cap slots; only UNSAFE ones get autoApplyHeld), L43 (casual-locked is a terminal ledger outcome), smine-skills L45 (the lockout drops candidates, never existing entries) and L59 (reconciliation drops only done/rejected/already-present entries), and smine-consolidate L39-40 (re-home into skills.json has no audience check).
